summary: Pierce County, WA summit with an L-4 cab built in 1933; cab removed or destroyed in 1965 (sources differ); now a hiking summit with no remains described.

facts.design: L-4 cab (Willhite describes the L-4 type as a 14x14 wood-frame cab with a hip roof)
facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in 1965; sources differ on which. Summit described as the spot of a former lookout with no remains described

access.note: Hiking summit reached by West Fork Road (FR 74) and a 1.5-mile hike; Willhite notes the White River bridge on the approach is washed out; page is undated and no closure is described

visit.trail_note: Hike of 1.5 miles with about 1,000 feet of gain, starting where the clear-cuts end (Willhite)

events.note: L-4 cab built in 1933 (Register and Willhite agree on the year)
George Clisby took panoramic photos from the cab roof on August 10, 1934
Register says removed in 1965; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1965; Willhite says thought destroyed in the mid-1960s
Registered May 22, 2012 as FFLOS US 1272, WA 172; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: L-4 cab built in 1933 and removed in 1965 (Register)
evidence.quote: Built in 1933, this L-4 cab was removed in 1965.

evidence.supports: firelookout.com gives 1933 L-4 cab and destroyed in 1965

evidence.quote: In 1933, an L-4 cab was built.

evidence.supports: Willhite: the cab is thought to have been destroyed in the mid-1960s
evidence.quote: In the mid-1960s, the cab is thought to have been destroyed.

evidence.supports: L-4 described as the most popular live-in lookout, a 14x14 wood-frame cab with a hip roof
evidence.quote: This was the most popular live-in lookout. It was a 14x14 wood frame cab that had a hip roof with 4 sides.

evidence.supports: George Clisby took panoramic photos from the roof on August 10, 1934
evidence.quote: On August 10, 1934, George Clisby took panoramic photos from the roof.

evidence.supports: one index places the site in the Snoqualmie National Forest
site in the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Pierce County
administered by the U.S. Forest Service
summit is a flat top, the spot of a former lookout
evidence.quote: The top is nice and flat, the spot of a former lookout tower.

evidence.supports: trail starts where the clear-cuts end
evidence.quote: The trail starts where the clear-cuts end.

evidence.supports: drive from Enumclaw on State Route 410 for 22 miles to West Fork Road (FR 74)
evidence.quote: From Enumclaw drive east on State Route 410 for 22 miles to a right onto West Fork Road (Forest Road 74).

evidence.supports: bridge over the White River is washed out (page update)
evidence.quote: The bridge over the White River is washed out.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says the cab was removed in 1965, firelookout.com says destroyed in 1965, and Willhite says thought destroyed in the mid-1960s. The story reports the disagreement and does not choose.
The Register and firelookout.com name the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest; the Forest Lookouts index names the Snoqualmie National Forest.

sources.title: Clear West Peak Fire Lookout Cabin

notes_for_editor: Brief lists kind 'ground'; sources give only an L-4 cab and do not say whether it stood on a tower, so the record's kind is unverified. Two searches found no staffing or fire records, so none are included. Access 'public' is inferred from a hiking description with an undated bridge note.
